Which of the following could represent the level curves of the surface $z=\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ shown above?
worked_solution:
First, notice that the range of $f(x,y)$ is $[-1,1].$ So, we will consider only $c$-level curves for $c\in [-1,1].$

The level curves for the function $f(x,y)$ are given by the equations 

$$
f(x,y)=c
$$

Therefore, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =c \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡y & =c \\ y & =\pm \operatorname{arccos}⁡c+2\pi n\end{aligned}
$$

where $n$ can be any integer. 

Notice that in the equations $y=\pm \operatorname{arccos}⁡c+2\pi n$ do not depend on $x.$ So, for a given $c\in [-1,1]$ and integer $n$, the right-hand side of the equation is constant. As a result, we obtain a family of horizontal lines, as shown below.
